analysis:
The PR changes documentation only. docs/architecture/security/attestation.md is the head-text excerpt for lines 263-543, with no visible patch hunk, so I found no concrete security change there. docs/architecture/security/identity-binding.md updates its date, clarifies that only protocol 3 is negotiated for Apple proof exchanges, and adds a 'Supervised App Attest worker candidate' section. That section describes a same-signed-executable child process for DeviceCheck calls: the parent keeps the X25519 endpoint key, exact-code and audit-token peer checks apply, the RPC is typed (no sign(hash)), and worker timeout/cancel retires the process before any replacement. It also states that the candidate defaults off and is not production-ready, that worker failure never falls back to in-process Apple calls or manufactures authorization, and that provider logout stops the process before revocation and local deletion, with only HTTP 204 treated as confirmation of remote revocation.

These claims are consistent with the canonical context (TB-011, TB-009, T-053, T-057, A-008, A-015, A-016). I found no weakening of any existing control, and no new unmitigated attack surface evident from the text. The doc cites provider-swift worker files that were not supplied, so the described controls are unverified. This is a coverage limit, not evidence of safety: the next pass should check the actual Worker/*.swift code and ProviderLoop+AppAttestWorker.swift if they are in the batch. In particular, check peer-token and code-identity enforcement, the one-use bootstrap secret, handling of the worker's credential state and lease, and the logout and revocation 204-only handling. Doc line references are stated but not verified.
